brief.t: A private bank started in 2004 by Rana Kapoor and Ashok Kapur; headquartered in Mumbai.
In March 2020 the RBI put it under a moratorium; an SBI-led group of banks rescued it, and Prashant Kumar led the turnaround as CEO until April 2026.
In September 2025 Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) bought over 24% and became the largest shareholder; SBI still holds about 10.8%.
Former SBI MD Vinay M. Tonse has been MD & CEO since 6 April 2026. FY 2025-26 profit rose 44.5% to ₹3,476 crore.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit rose 65% to ₹1,080 crore, but in October 2026 the Supreme Court struck down the 2020 write-off of ₹8,415 crore of AT-1 bonds, a big capital question.

timeline.t: YES Bank started, founded by Rana Kapoor and Ashok Kapur.
RBI moratorium; SBI-led rescue; Prashant Kumar became administrator, then MD & CEO.
SMBC became the largest shareholder, buying stakes from SBI, other banks and a Carlyle affiliate.
Added to the Nifty Bank index.
Vinay M. Tonse took charge as MD & CEO.
Supreme Court upheld the order quashing the ₹8,415 crore AT-1 bond write-off.

model.how: YES Bank earns mainly from the gap between interest on loans and interest paid on deposits, plus fees. It lends to companies, small businesses and retail customers, and is now growing its low-cost savings and current account deposits.
flow: Bank lends to companies, MSMEs and individuals

points: RBI must approve a private bank's CEO and Chairman; YES Bank changed its CEO in April 2026.
RBI approval is also needed for any investor to buy 5% or more of a bank; SMBC got approval to go up to 24.99%.
Big theme for interviews: how a failed bank was rescued, and how court rulings on bonds affect bank capital.

frameworks.note: Framework views are analysis built from the verified facts on this page, not company statements.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.AT-1 bond: Additional Tier-1 bond: a special bond that counts as bank capital and can be written off if the bank fails. YES Bank's ₹8,415 crore AT-1 write-off in 2020 was struck down by the courts.
glossary.Moratorium: A temporary freeze set by the RBI on a troubled bank's payments and withdrawals while it is rescued.
glossary.CET1 ratio: Common Equity Tier 1: the bank's core capital (mainly shareholders' money) as a share of its risk-weighted loans.

Role knowledge, the bank and HR questions

Finance.q: What is an AT-1 bond, and why does the Supreme Court ruling matter for YES Bank?
Finance.a: AT-1 bonds count as bank capital. The 2020 write-off of ₹8,415 cr was struck down, so the bank may have to restore them, which could cut its CET1 ratio by about 2.5 percentage points.

Finance.q: YES Bank's profit rose 44.5% in FY26. What drove it?
Finance.a: Higher net interest income, better margins, lower bad loans (Gross NPA 1.3%) and lower costs as a share of income.

Finance.q: Why is YES Bank's margin lower than many private banks?
Finance.a: It carries more low-yield corporate loans and mandated RIDF deposits from its past; it is shifting to retail and low-cost CASA deposits.

Marketing.q: How would you rebuild the YES Bank brand after the 2020 crisis?
Marketing.a: Highlight the turnaround, strong backers like SMBC and SBI, low bad loans and good service, through simple, honest campaigns.

Marketing.q: How can YES Bank use its SMBC link in marketing?
Marketing.a: Target Japanese and global companies in India and position the bank as having global strength with local reach.

HR.q: How would you keep staff motivated through a leadership change?
HR.a: Clear communication from the new CEO, stable goals, recognition and steady training.

Sales.q: A customer remembers the 2020 moratorium. How do you reassure them?
Sales.a: Acknowledge it honestly; explain the rescue, RBI regulation, deposit insurance basics, strong shareholders and today's profits.

Operations.q: How would you help a bank grow its branch network quickly?
Operations.a: Choose locations with data, standardise set-up, train staff early and track each new branch's results.

interview.why_us: YES Bank is one of India's most interesting turnaround stories: rescued in 2020, it grew profit 44.5% in FY26 and 65% last quarter, now has Japan's SMBC as its largest shareholder and a new CEO. Joining now means learning how a bank rebuilds and grows. I want to contribute to [your role] in this next phase.

gd.t: Was it right to write off YES Bank's AT-1 bonds in 2020?
gd.for: It saved the bank and protected depositors.
gd.against: The Supreme Court found the write-off was not valid; investors' rights matter too.

gd.t: Should foreign banks own large stakes in Indian banks?
gd.for: They bring capital, skills and global links, like SMBC at YES Bank.
gd.against: Key banks may be influenced by foreign priorities.
